context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System processes card-not-present payment authorizations in AWS (`eu-west-1`) to detect fraud and support analyst reviews. It balances strict sub-50ms P99 latency requirements at 3,000 TPS with PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year immutable audit constraint.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Core Ledger (Source of authorization requests)
- Fraud Analysts (System users for case management)
- Card Schemes / Issuer 3DS Directory Servers (EMVCo 3DS 2.x APIs)
- ML Feature Store / Threat Intelligence Provider (External IP/device fingerprinting APIs)
- Identity Provider (IdP for authentication and RBAC)
- Notification Service (Email/SMS alerts)
- Model Training & Experimentation Environment (Amazon SageMaker Studio)
- AWS CloudFront & ALB (Perimeter ingress)
- AWS KMS & S3 Object Lock (Cryptographic audit and storage)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to System: Ingress via gRPC over HTTP/2 with mTLS (3,000 TPS)
- Fraud Analysts to CloudFront/ALB: Ingress via HTTPS (TLS 1.3) with AWS WAF protection
- System to Card Schemes / Feature Store: Outbound egress via HTTPS
- System to S3 Object Lock / KMS: Tamper-evident 7-year audit logging and encryption via AWS IAM policies
- Training Environment to System: Secure, signed model artifact transfer via AWS S3 Cross-Account Policies

## Technology Stack
- AWS (`eu-west-1`): Cloud infrastructure provider chosen for managed compliance and regional data residency
- gRPC over HTTP/2: Low-latency transport protocol meeting the <50ms P99 SLA at 3,000 TPS
- AWS CloudFront, ALB & WAF: Perimeter security, TLS 1.3 termination, and DDoS mitigation
- AWS KMS & S3 Object Lock: Tamper-evident, immutable 7-year audit data storage (R-06)
- Amazon SageMaker Studio: Out-of-band model development and zero-downtime updates (R-03)
- AWS Secrets Manager: Automated credential rotation for PCI-DSS compliance

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to meet stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability constraints without exceeding a three-engineer team capacity. High-throughput gRPC communication and serverless edge components ensure P99 latency remains under 50 ms at 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud within milliseconds and manages suspicious payment reviews. It is architected as a secure, low-maintenance cloud system optimized for a three-engineer team within a fixed budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Scoring Engine Container
- Case Management Backend Container
- Tokenization Proxy Container
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon S3 Object Lock

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts interact with Case Management Backend via AWS ALB using HTTPS.
- AWS ALB routes external authorization traffic to Scoring Engine via HTTPS/gRPC.
- Scoring Engine communicates with external Feature Stores via gRPC.
- Scoring Engine writes hot state to Amazon DynamoDB and audit logs to Amazon S3 Object Lock via AWS SDK.
- Case Management Backend reads and writes investigation data to Amazon DynamoDB via VPC Endpoints.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS Fargate:** Serverless container orchestration chosen to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team.
- **Go:** Programming language for the Scoring Engine to ensure sub-50ms P99 latency and predictable memory footprints.
- **ONNX Runtime:** Embedded C++ scoring engine within Go for zero-downtime model updates.
- **Node.js / TypeScript:** Backend framework for case management workflows.
- **AWS Nitro Enclaves:** Hardware-level isolation for tokenization to ensure PCI-DSS compliance and protect card data.
- **Amazon S3 Object Lock:** Compliance-mode storage ensuring tamper-evident 7-year audit retention.
- **AWS ALB Circuit Breaker:** Edge-level fail-open mechanism ensuring availability constraints during outages.

## Rationale
This architecture meets sub-50ms latency and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security requirements by combining high-performance Go/ONNX scoring with isolated tokenization proxies. It respects budget and operational constraints by utilizing serverless AWS primitives that require minimal maintenance from a three-engineer team.

AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB).analysis:
## Overview
The system is a Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening platform that screens card-not-present payment authorizations and manages suspicious payment reviews. It provides sub-50ms latency, PCI-DSS compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Listener Component (AWS ALB Listener)
- Routing Rules Engine
- Health Check & Circuit Breaker Component
- WAF & Security Filter Component (AWS WAF)
- Access Logging & Telemetry Component
- Target Group Manager
- Scoring Engine Container (Go, ONNX Runtime, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend Container (Node.js, TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Tokenization Proxy Container (AWS Nitro Enclaves)
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon S3 Object Lock

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Core Ledger -> Listener Component: Routes external authorization traffic [HTTPS/gRPC]
- Fraud Analysts -> Listener Component: Interacts with Case Management Backend [HTTPS]
- Listener Component -> WAF & Security Filter Component: Inspects headers and payloads [In-Memory]
- Listener Component -> Routing Rules Engine: Internal handoff [In-Memory]
- Routing Rules Engine -> Case Management Backend Container: Routes analyst traffic [HTTPS]
- Routing Rules Engine -> Scoring Engine Container: Forwards authorization traffic [gRPC over HTTP/2]
- Routing Rules Engine -> Tokenization Proxy Container: Forwards raw card payloads [gRPC over HTTP/2]
- Routing Rules Engine -> Access Logging & Telemetry Component: Emits metadata asynchronously [In-Memory/Queue]
- Routing Rules Engine -> Target Group Manager: Resolves backend ECS tasks [In-Memory]
- Target Group Manager -> Scoring Engine Container: Manages connection pools [gRPC over HTTP/2]
- Health Check & Circuit Breaker Component -> Scoring Engine Container: Performs active health probes [HTTP GET]
- Access Logging & Telemetry Component -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Stores audit logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Application Load Balancer: Edge routing, TLS termination, and traffic splitting within infrastructure budget.
- AWS WAF: Managed security filtering for OWASP Top 10 protection to minimize operational toil for a 3-engineer team.
- gRPC over HTTP/2: Internal protocol for low-latency communication satisfying the P99 < 50ms requirement (R-04).
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Tamper-evident immutable storage meeting the 7-year auditability constraint (R-06).
- AWS Nitro Enclaves: Isolated compute environment ensuring tokenized card data security for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS cloud services to maintain a fixed infrastructure budget of 25,000 EUR per month and support a three-engineer operational model. Asynchronous logging and gRPC protocols ensure strict sub-50ms latency (R-04) while meeting PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability requirements.

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time payment fraud screening for card-not-present transactions, evaluating authorizations and managing reviews while ensuring strict compliance. It processes up to 3,000 requests per second within sub-50ms latencies on AWS.

## Key Elements
- API Handler Component (Go, net/http / gRPC)
- Sanitization & Tokenization Guard Component (Go)
- Feature Fetcher Component (Go concurrency primitives)
- Circuit Breaker & Fallback Component (Go)
- Inference Engine Component (C++ via cgo, ONNX Runtime)
- Model Loader Component (Go)
- Decision Explainer Component (Go)
- Audit & Persistence Component (Go, AWS SDK)
- External Systems: AWS ALB, ML Feature Store, Tokenization Proxy Container (AWS Nitro Enclaves), Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon S3 Object Lock

## Relationships
- AWS ALB -> API Handler Component: Routes external authorization traffic [HTTPS/gRPC]
- API Handler Component -> Sanitization & Tokenization Guard Component: Internal Go call
- Sanitization & Tokenization Guard Component -> Tokenization Proxy Container: Tokenizes card data [gRPC/mTLS over internal VPC]
- Feature Fetcher Component -> ML Feature Store: Retrieves real-time features [gRPC]
- Feature Fetcher Component -> Circuit Breaker & Fallback Component: Go error handling / interface call
- Circuit Breaker & Fallback Component -> Inference Engine Component: Passes feature vector [Go function call]
- Model Loader Component -> Inference Engine Component: Hot-swaps models [In-memory pointer swap]
- Inference Engine Component -> Decision Explainer Component: In-memory Go struct passing
- Decision Explainer Component -> Audit & Persistence Component: Asynchronous event emission via Go channel
- Audit & Persistence Component -> Amazon DynamoDB / Amazon S3 Object Lock: Writes hot state and tamper-evident audit logs [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high concurrency and low-latency API handling and feature orchestration.
- C++ via cgo & ONNX Runtime: Executes compiled fraud scoring models in-memory for microsecond-level latency.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Provides a fixed-budget, serverless container execution environment.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock & DynamoDB: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year audit log retention for regulatory compliance.
- AWS Nitro Enclaves: Isolates tokenization to achieve PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages in-memory C++ inference and asynchronous logging to consistently achieve sub-50ms P99 latency under high throughput. Isolated tokenization enclaves and tamper-evident S3 storage satisfy stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 and auditability mandates within a fixed budget.

Tokenization Proxy Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Tokenization Proxy Container provides hardware-isolated card data tokenization within an AWS Nitro Enclave to ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It securely processes payment payloads while maintaining sub-50ms P99 latency and a stateless memory footprint.

## Key Elements
- API Router: Rust (Hyper/Tokio) component handling gRPC request termination over vsock.
- Tokenization Core: Rust component managing ephemeral AES-GCM DEKs, `moka` in-memory LRU cache, and AWS KMS integration.
- Audit Logger: Rust component generating and forwarding cryptographic hashes for tamper-evident logging.
- Health & Attestation Monitor: Rust component managing cryptographic attestation and vsock health checks.
- Parent ECS Task: Orchestrator managing network and storage handoffs.

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine Container -> `gRPC over VSOCK` -> API Router: Sends cleartext PAN for tokenization/detokenization.
- Tokenization Core -> `HTTPS (TLS 1.3)` -> AWS KMS: Performs envelope encryption via parent VPC endpoint.
- Audit Logger -> `gRPC over VSOCK` -> Parent ECS Task: Streams tamper-evident audit hashes for S3 Object Lock ingestion.

## Technology Stack
- Rust (Hyper/Tokio): Chosen for memory safety and high-throughput concurrency within a small engineering team.
- AWS Nitro Enclaves: Selected for hardware-level isolation to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 requirements.
- VSOCK / gRPC: Used for internal secure communication, eliminating network attack surfaces.
- `moka` LRU Cache: Provides volatile memory caching for sub-millisecond data retrieval to meet the 50ms P99 latency budget.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict hardware isolation and zero disk persistence to meet compliance mandates within a fixed budget. Utilizing a unified Rust technology stack and in-memory caching ensures low latency while minimizing maintenance overhead for a three-person engineering team.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time card-not-present payment fraud screening and case management for a mid-size payment processor. It screens payment authorizations in real-time while ensuring strict PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- **Hot State Table Module**: DynamoDB provisioned capacity table storing transaction velocity counters and card profiles.
- **Case Management Table Module**: DynamoDB on-demand capacity table storing analyst investigation cases and audit logs.
- **DynamoDB Streams Processor**: AWS Lambda function capturing mutation events for downstream audit export.
- **Audit Ledger Archive Module**: Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) for immutable 7-year retention.
- **IAM Fine-Grained Access Policy Module**: AWS IAM enforcing least-privilege attribute-based access control (ABAC).
- **Global Table Replication Module**: DynamoDB Global Tables ensuring multi-AZ resilience in `eu-west-1`.
- **Time-To-Live (TTL) Expiry Module**: Native DynamoDB background process purging transient records.
- **DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) Module**: Continuous backup module for investigation logs.

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine Container -> Hot State Table Module: Reads/Writes velocity state via *AWS SDK (TCP/443 via VPC Endpoint)*.
- Case Management Backend Container -> Case Management Table Module: Reads/Writes case data via *AWS SDK (TCP/443)*.
- Hot State Table Module -> DynamoDB Streams Processor: Triggers audit logging via *DynamoDB Streams*.
- DynamoDB Streams Processor -> Audit Ledger Archive Module: Flushes encrypted mutation logs via *AWS SDK (HTTPS)*.
- Case Management Table Module -> AWS KMS: Encrypts data at rest via *AWS KMS CMK (Envelope Encryption)*.
- IAM Fine-Grained Access Policy Module -> Hot State Table Module: Secures access boundaries via *IAM Policies*.
- Hot State Table Module -> TTL Expiry Module: Automatically purges expired records via *Native DynamoDB TTL background process*.
- Case Management Table Module -> DynamoDB PITR Module: Continuously backs up logs via *DynamoDB PITR*.

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon DynamoDB**: Chosen for single-digit millisecond latency (R-04) without the operational overhead of DAX.
- **AWS Lambda**: Chosen for serverless execution of mutation capture without managing compute infrastructure.
- **Amazon S3 Object Lock**: Chosen for immutable, tamper-evident 7-year audit retention (R-06).
- **AWS KMS**: Chosen for envelope encryption to satisfy PCI-DSS data security constraints (R-05).

## Rationale
The architecture uses fully managed AWS services to meet strict performance and compliance mandates while respecting a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It limits operational toil, enabling a three-engineer team to maintain high availability and security.

Amazon S3 Object Lock.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real-time for fraud and provides case management for human analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and tamper-evident 7-year audit retention on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts
- Scoring Engine Container (Go, ONNX Runtime, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend Container (Node.js, TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon S3 Object Lock Container (Compliance Mode, S3 Glacier Deep Archive)
- Internal Components: Object Writer, Lifecycle Management, Audit Verification, Access Control & Compliance Policy Manager, Metadata Indexer
- Supporting Services: Amazon DynamoDB, AWS KMS, Amazon SQS/SNS

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine Container -> Object Writer Component: Writes decision payloads [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Case Management Backend Container -> Object Writer Component: Writes human review audit trails [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Object Writer Component -> AWS S3 Storage Layer: Persists immutable objects [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Lifecycle Management Component -> AWS S3 Storage Layer: Configures transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Audit Verification Component -> AWS S3 Storage Layer: Reads and verifies object integrity [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Access Control & Compliance Policy Manager -> AWS S3 Storage Layer: Configures bucket compliance parameters [AWS IAM / AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Access Control & Compliance Policy Manager -> AWS KMS: Enforces server-side encryption [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- AWS S3 Storage Layer -> Metadata Indexer Component: Triggers event notifications [S3 Event Notifications, HTTPS]
- Metadata Indexer Component -> Amazon DynamoDB: Persists audit metadata pointers [AWS SDK, HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode: Ensures immutable, tamper-evident 7-year retention (R-06)
- S3 Glacier Deep Archive: Optimizes storage costs to meet the 25,000 EUR/month budget
- AWS KMS: Encrypts data at rest for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance (R-05)
- Amazon DynamoDB & SQS/SNS: Indexes audit metadata for rapid auditor querying without full-bucket scans
- AWS SDK (HTTPS): Protocol for secure intra-container and AWS service communication

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS cloud services to meet strict PCI-DSS and 7-year auditability mandates while staying within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and supporting a 3-engineer team. Automated tiering and indexing balance deep storage compliance with high-performance query access.
